Texas A&M International University students are offering free health screenings to the public for the first time at the university's Clinical Health Sciences Center, according to KGNS (Oct. 21, 2026).

Students majoring in kinesiology and communication sciences and disorders staffed the clinic from 1 to 5 p.m. on Wednesday, performing services ranging from voice evaluations to body composition assessments — practicing their clinical skills while providing free resources to the city.

Yaritza Gonzalez, a TAMIU junior studying kinesiology, told KGNS the opportunity is about serving Laredo families in need, saying she wants to "give back to the community" and noting that many local families are less funded and could use these opportunities.

Dr. Jose Moris, a health science professor, said the university plans to keep offering the free services every semester. The arrangement, he said, is a win on both sides: students get trained to run real clinical services while the community benefits.

The need is real. According to the Gateway Community Health Center, Laredo is one of the fastest-growing cities in Texas, and Webb County is designated as both a medically underserved area and a health professional shortage area — leaving many families without access to needed care.

TAMIU senior Anel Espinoza said taking part matters to her because Laredo faces a shortage of speech therapists, and her program aims to train more of them for the community.

Anyone interested in a free screening can stop by the Clinical Health Sciences Center at 5201 University Blvd. from 1 to 5 p.m. through Thursday, Oct. 22. TAMIU's own newsroom had announced the faculty-and-student screenings for Oct. 21–22 earlier this month.

Sources: KGNS, "TAMIU students offer free health screenings in Laredo" (Oct. 21, 2026); Texas A&M International University (tamiu.edu).
